YOUR AUTOGENIC TRAINING
Choose a Module
SubCat01_Text:
Autogenic Training is a scientifically recognized relaxation method developed in the 1920s by the Berlin psychiatrist Johannes Heinrich Schultz. It is based on self-suggestion: by repeatedly mentally reciting certain formulas ("My arm is very heavy", "My breathing is calm and even"), one puts body and mind into a state of deep relaxation.

Effects on Body and Mind
Autogenic Training can reduce stress, relieve inner tension, and enhance concentration. When practiced regularly, it supports regeneration, improves sleep, and can alleviate psychosomatic complaints. On a mental level, it helps to organize thoughts, find inner calm, and enhance well-being. Influence on the Autonomic Nervous System The autonomic nervous system controls vital bodily functions such as heart rate, breathing, blood pressure, and digestion – largely without our conscious intervention. Autogenic Training has a regulating effect on this system by activating the parasympathetic nervous system, which is responsible for relaxation and recovery. At the same time, the excessive activity of the sympathetic nervous system – responsible for stress reactions such as rapid heartbeat or muscle tension – is reduced. Examples of Control through Autogenic Training
  • Cardiovascular System: By using the formula 'My heart beats calmly and regularly', pulse rate can decrease, and blood pressure and heart rate stabilize.
  • Breathing: With 'My breathing flows calmly and evenly', breathing can be deepened and slowed, promoting inner calm.
  • Muscles: 'My arms and legs are pleasantly heavy' can relieve muscle tension and induce physical relaxation.
  • Temperature Regulation: 'My right arm is very warm' influences blood circulation and can warm cold hands or feet. Through this self-regulation, Autogenic Training becomes an effective tool for bringing body and mind into harmony and building long-term stress resistance.
SubCat02_Instruction: Select individual basic exercises of Autogenic Training to deepen them. The exercises build on each other and should be performed in the specified order.
